message: We have twenty signed-in staff and three reviewers, with approval forbidden for ordinary uploaders, alongside the stated PDF, volume and retention limits. Let’s make that separation explicit in the application and require denied-approval tests; accounting residency and Sydney placement remain unresolved.

proposal.title: Separate invoice upload and reviewer permissions
proposal.body: Record the stated staff and reviewer populations and enforce approval permissions within the existing composed workflow. Preserve the current scope, connections and layout; Australian residency remains required, Sydney remains proposed, and accounting compatibility remains unverified.

next.name: Asynchronous document intake
next.requirements: Users upload PDF invoices. Extract the supplier, invoice date, total and currency into a review queue. Delivery can repeat; retries must not create duplicate invoices. A reviewer approves a result before it is sent to our existing accounting API. Use AWS. Recommend a coherent system and the engineering choices. Ask only a small material business question when needed; do not make me configure the system.

data.label: Invoice upload and review
data.description: Existing staff browser outside provisioning scope. Serves twenty signed-in staff and three reviewers; whether these populations overlap is unspecified. Staff upload PDF invoices and inspect extracted fields alongside source evidence. Only authorized reviewers may approve a specific result revision; ordinary uploaders cannot approve. Authentication and application reviewer membership are separate controls enforced by the workflow server.

data.label: Invoice processing and approval
data.description: Composed invoice-workflow deployment unit on Amazon ECS. Owns browser/API, background worker, isolated PDF/OCR parser, private versioned Amazon S3 originals, durable PostgreSQL queue/outbox on Amazon RDS, staff sign-in, SQL user/reviewer membership, regional model integration, separate workload identities and operating tasks/monitoring. Serves twenty signed-in staff and three reviewers; population overlap is unspecified. Enforce reviewer authorization server-side on every approval operation: ordinary uploaders cannot approve, including through direct API requests. Propose acceptance tests for unauthenticated access, uploader approval denial and authorized reviewer approval bound to an exact revision. Accepts PDFs up to 10,000,000 bytes; the proposed 100-page safeguard remains reviewable. Plans for approximately 500 invoices/day; 15,000/month assumes 30 intake days and is not measured usage. Invoices may contain personal data. Extracts supplier, invoice date, total and currency with source evidence into a durable review queue. Approval binds the exact result revision, source and destination contract; model output cannot authorize delivery. Transactional job creation, fenced worker leases and bounded retries preserve processing across failures. Accounting sends use stable operation and payload identity; uncertain outcomes are fenced for reconciliation rather than blindly resent. Destination must independently pass normalized-action-v1 and idempotency acceptance. Retain originals and extraction audit history for 90 days. Implement scheduled cleanup and review versions, backups and restore behavior against that requirement; retention eligibility alone does not prove erasure. Propose Sydney ap-southeast-2, not yet user-approved, with documents, extracted data, model processing, logs containing invoice data, backups and state restricted to Australia. No silent overseas inference or recovery fallback. Propose encryption, authorized staff/reviewer access and exclusion of invoice content from operational logs. Accounting residency is unresolved. Service/model availability, quotas, model data-retention policy, destination connectivity, build/scan evidence, restore and alert delivery remain unverified.

data.label: Existing accounting API
data.description: Client-owned existing accounting service, referenced without recreation or modification. Receives only approved invoice results. Vendor, hosting and processing locations, authentication and retention behavior are unknown; Australian residency must be established before sending invoice data. Its adapter must pass normalized-action-v1 acceptance, including durable idempotency for repeated operation IDs and reconciliation after ambiguous responses. Compatibility and residency are not established by this diagram.

requirementUpdates.rationale: Make the explicit access boundary enforceable at the server rather than relying on hidden browser controls; preserve the existing revision-bound approval safeguards as proposed controls.
requirementUpdates.statement: Support twenty signed-in staff and three reviewers. Ordinary uploaders must not approve invoices; only authorized reviewers may approve an exact result revision before accounting delivery. Proposed controls bind approval to the source and destination contract, invalidate approval when the result changes and retain attributable approval/delivery history. Verify approval denial through direct API requests as well as the browser.
requirementUpdates.sourceText: Twenty signed-in staff and three reviewers; ordinary uploaders cannot approve.

requirementUpdates.rationale: Preserve the stated intake baseline without inferring peak demand or a processing deadline.
requirementUpdates.statement: Accept PDF invoices up to 10 MB and support approximately 500 invoices per day through durable intake, extraction and review without losing accepted work. Validate with representative PDFs and failure recovery; peak demand and processing latency remain unspecified.
requirementUpdates.sourceText: PDF invoices up to 10 MB, around 500 per day; they may contain personal data.

requirementUpdates.rationale: Retain the explicit retention duration while keeping unresolved deletion and backup semantics visible.
requirementUpdates.statement: Retain invoice originals and extraction audit history for 90 days. Proposed implementation includes cleanup across application records and object versions, documented backup expiry and restoration handling. The retention start event and exact deletion deadline remain unresolved.
requirementUpdates.sourceText: Keep originals and extraction audit history for 90 days.

Explain missing controls and tests. Propose requirements from the components and paths; mark default targets as suggestions, never existing company policy.

skills.name: AWS architecture guidance
skills.summary: Apply AWS Well-Architected concerns to the drawn workload with evidence. Distinguish Bedrock on-demand model access, knowledge-base/vector storage, guardrails and IAM; they are separate concerns. S3 storage, requests and transfer are separate cost dimensions. A diagram is not a complete Well-Architected review. Native generation currently covers only S3 foundations.
